title: BEAT: Boundary-aware Efficient Anatomy-Transfer for Multimodal Mitral Valve Segmentation
abstract:
Mitral valve repair is planned and guided by three very different images of the same anatomy: preoperative cardiac computed tomography (CT), intraoperative 3D transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE), and the surgeon's view of the valve. Delineating the valve consistently in all three is the perception layer on which a patient-specific valve model rests, yet annotations are scarce and the gap between modalities is wide. We introduce \textbf{BEAT}, a boundary-aware efficient anatomy-transfer recipe instantiated once per modality: a CT-pretrained STU-Net for the volumetric tasks and an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet for video, train-only distance and topology losses, augmentation matched to the physical shift, and every expensive component confined to training, leaving a single-pass model that segments a CT case in 0.34~s with 1.4~GiB. On the MICCAI 2026 MVAA challenge, BEAT achieves Dice 0.85 on CT, 0.83 on 3D TEE, and 0.77 on surgical video. Ablations read against fold and seed variation show what carries each modality: transfer on video, physics-matched augmentation on ultrasound, and a post-processing rule that never erases a weak prediction.
\keywords{Mitral valve \and Multimodal segmentation \and Domain generalization \and Semi-supervised learning.}
